description:
The NSLS-II beamlines provide world-class facilities for research. The increased brilliance of the source, along with automation for data analysis has led to a significant increase in the acquisition speed and the amount of data which must be processed and analyzed by NSLS-II users. It is therefore essential to provide advanced tools making use of artificial intelligence and machine learning for data acquisition and data analysis and to work with the diverse user community of the NSLS-II in developing these tools.
 NSLS-II has initiated AI pilot programs to further the development of these techniques. We are looking to recruit a scientist to work on Ai and machine learning developments for synchrotron applications, notably for applications where data analysis and management coupled with automated data collection would provide a large benefit to the experimental process.
 The work will take place the Data Science and Systems Integration (DSSI) in close collaboration with beamlines beamline groups.
 
 Essential Duties and Responsibilities: 
 Development of innovative machine-learning based algorithms for data acquisition and online data processing.

 Organize data, meta-data standards, provide mechanisms for distributing data and analysis tools for integration of NSLS-II results in a broader context.

 Conduct original research project exploiting machine learning for synchrotron applications with NSLS-II science programs.

 Work with scientists and engineers at NSLS-II, user groups and research sponsors to disseminate knowledge about the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning for light source science applications.

 
 Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: 
 PhD degree in Physics, Biology, Computer Science, Science or similar area

 At least 10 years of experience in synchrotron light source science.

 Curiosity, good communication skills and ability to work in large multi-disciplinary teams.

 
 Preferred Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: 
 Demonstration of the deployment machine (deep) learning developments ideally for synchrotron data analysis or similar

 Strong programming skills in Python GPU programming (CUDA, OpenCL) is a plus.

 Experience in working with collaborative open-source projects for science and/or engineering.

 
 Brookhaven National Laboratory is committed to providing fair, equitable and competitive compensation. The full salary range for this position is $154,250.00 - $235,000.00 / year. Salary offers will be commensurate with the final candidate’s qualification, education and experience and considered with the internal peer group.  

 Brookhaven National Laboratory is committed to employee success and we believe that a comprehensive employee benefits program is an important and meaningful part of the compensation employees receive. Review more information at BNL | Benefits Program 

 Brookhaven National Laboratory requires all non-badged personnel including visitors to produce a REAL-ID or REAL-ID compliant documentation to access Brookhaven National Laboratory – view more information at  www.bnl.gov/real-id .  This is due to nationwide identification requirements for federal site access as required by the federal  REAL ID Act .   Those not in possession of a REAL ID-compliant document will not be permitted to access the site which includes access to the Laboratory for interviews . 

 As a U.S. Department of Energy laboratory, Brookhaven National Laboratory requires employees to obtain and maintain a DOE Uncleared Personal Identity Verification (UPIV) credential in accordance with Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) requirements. The credentialing process is completed as part of onboarding and enables access to DOE facilities and information systems. As a condition of employment, the selected candidate must be able to obtain and maintain a UPIV credential. These requirements are established under DOE Order 206.2 Chg. 2, Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM- Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) ) , and DOE Order 473.1A- Physical Protection Program- Physical Protection Program .

 About Us 
 Brookhaven National Laboratory (www.bnl.gov) delivers discovery science and transformative technology to power and secure the nation’s future. Brookhaven Lab is a multidisciplinary laboratory with seven Nobel Prize-winning discoveries, 37 R&D 100 Awards, and more than 70 years of pioneering research. The Lab is primarily supported by the U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Science. Brookhaven Science Associates (BSA) operates and manages the Laboratory for DOE. BSA is a partnership between Battelle and The Research Foundation for the State University of New York on behalf of Stony Brook University. BSA salutes our veterans and active military members with careers that leverage the skills and unique experience they gained while serving our country, learn more at BNL | Opportunities for Veterans at Brookhaven National Laboratory .
